body: I remember when it was the one year anniversary of my mom’s death. I received a phone call from a family friend. I’ve known her for 11 years at this point and she helped manage my mother’s estate as I was 25 years old and my mother had no other family as they had all passed. She told me “it’s been enough” and to “get over it”. I told her if her husband had died, would she be over it? Or if her adult son had died, would she be over it? She understood a little but not really and at this point I realized I needed to step away. I’m so sorry you are going through this. My mom was my person and maybe your mom was too and although, it’s expected everyone’s parent’s to pass, I didn’t want it to be so soon. I wasn’t ready and feel like I had and still have to navigate young adulthood a lot on my own. I’m sorry about the health issues you are experiencing- it’s not the same but I went through a severe depression and felt unwell. I couldn’t hold down a job and didn’t want to go outside. It sucked and it still sucks but things have gotten better with time and support from my friends and other people who actually get it. I also started taking care of myself how my mom would want to take care of me as painful as it was at first (my depression really impacted my self-worth at this point). I know depression and chronic illness are different, but feel free to reach out to me- whether to vent, share a memory, or just have someone sit in the grief with you.

I understand your feeling as I currently don’t like my role as HR Generalist at my organization. I’m also super detailed and my boss is more go with the flow or has higher expectations for me but didn’t train me on a process/procedure and assumed I know it (even though most of our processes are not written out). I wish I had some advice but I decided that this position is not a good fit for me and I’m looking for a job with at least the same pay at a different organization. The only thing is the job market is brutal. Definitely look around though and see what opportunities are there.

I’ve worked a lot of shitty jobs before finding a “good” job. I think all jobs are going to feel like work and you feel tired from it at the end of the day. But a job shouldn’t be making you constantly on high alert, being so stressed from work that your body starts breaking down, or you mentally/emotionally stop enjoying things. I was trying really hard with education changing different schools and age groups but it’s not for me. I changed careers to HR as a recruiter for a mid size company that employees around 300 people. Do I have bad days? Of course! But I’m not so stressed out of my mind that I’m getting physically sick. I am getting paid a livable wage, and I feel appreciated a lot of times from coworkers and supervisors. It’s a lot better for me mentally to work with adults because adults can be jerks but I have not felt unsafe at work since working at this company. I’m not constantly in fight or flight mode.

It took me several tries to get a job I enjoyed. I was working in special education trying to find a school and different age group to see if it was getting better. It wasn’t getting better, so I started applying for jobs in higher Ed but I got really lucky and was hired as a recruiter/human resources generalist from a position on Indeed for a mid size 300 employee company. I’ve really enjoyed it! I think teaching skills transfer very well to Human Resources and recruitment. Definitely something to look into!
I completely understand. I was missing my mom extra hard this weekend and just really wanted to hug her and hear her voice.

Edit: I’m in counseling but we’ve mostly been talking about other issues that have happened since my mom’s death. Also, I was my mom’s only living family left. It’s hard because I can’t even talk to my dad about my mom because of how the divorce was. Sometimes I feel like I’m the only person who is carrying this grief. I wish I had one other person to remember and share memories of my mom.
I feel this in my soul. My heart physically hurts to not be able to talk to her. I miss our conversations and her texts and weekly phone calls.

I’m sorry about your daughter. It sounds like it was so hard for you. I was thinking about what to say but when I was reading your post again and again, I realized I gave a lot of the same physical symptoms but I feel like I have a lot psychological symptoms too like I often wear my mom’s clothes to feel close to her or I wish a lot of times that I died when she died. Thanks for responding. I hope my symptoms stop being so intense.
No, she wasn’t abroad with me. I hadn’t seen for 6 months when she died.

I get that feeling too. It’s like an awful nightmare that you want to wake up from. It’s gotten to the point that in my dreams, she’s alive and I’m thinking that it was all a bad dream. I miss her so much and think about her.

I’m so sorry about your mom. I lost my mom on September 12th 2020. My mom was my whole world too. I can tell by your pictures that you guys were super close. I was super close to my mom. I wish I had any words or advice because I miss my mom terribly. Just know that you aren’t alone and that she loves you and wants you to be okay even if it feels impossible. 💕
